title.narrative: A program for improving the quality, transparency and efficiency of administrative public services developed

baseline.value: Multiple, sometimes overlapping or conflicting, services provided by various government entities in a non-transparent, inefficientand customer unfriendly manner.

comment.narrative: New indicator, added at the stage of approval of additional grant financing in December 2012

target.value: A program for improving the quality, transparency and efficiency of administrative public services at national and sub-nationallevels developed. New service delivery model piloted in three rayons.

actual.value: Review of administrative services provided at the central level completed. 568 services catalogued, recommendations onreorganizing, merging, and discontinuing services developed. The development of the program for improving the quality, transparencyand efficiency of administrative public services at national and sub-national levels is ongoing. New service delivery model isbeing piloted in three ministries.

comment.narrative: Indicator expected toe b achieved by the project closing date

title.narrative: Reorganization of public administration has taken place in line with the principle of functional delineation and matching the role of government underpinned by national strategic documents

baseline.value: Policy and implementation functions are not well allocated. Staffing levels and resources do not match government strategies.

target.value: Recommendations for functional allocations in line with good governance principles and government strategies are formulated andreorganization plan is endorsed

actual.value: Reorganization of the Government in winter-spring 2010 took into account the recommendations of the earlier functional reviewssupported by the project and followed the principles of functional delineation and focus on strategic priorities. Law onGovernment amended and competencies delimited. Number of Central Public Administration bodies reduced from 29 to 24, number ofagencies reduced from 16 to 8. Government strategic planning committee has been re-established and is functioning.

title.narrative: The system of management of public administration reform is institutionalized

baseline.value: The Government does not have institutional capacity to implement public administration reform

target.value: Sustainable capacity to implement public administration reform is established. Units set up, staffed and trained.

actual.value: The capacity of State Chancellery for public administration reform management has improved after its 2010 reorganization. Centraldivision for policy coordination was strengthened and formally assigned the responsibility for managing public administrationreform under the leadership of the Secretary General of the State Chancellery.

title.narrative: Legal basis for organization and functioning of public administration has been developed and approved

baseline.value: There is no any legal act that stipulates the principles of organization of public administration, including structuring andaccountability

target.value: A law on public administration is approved and enforced

actual.value: The law on public administration has been approved by Parliament in April 2012

baseline.value: 1995 law on civil service does not meet criteria o competitive merit-based selection. Political and administrative positions arenot clearly separated.

target.value: The new Civil Service Law, compatible with EU practices, is approved by Parliament and enters into force.

actual.value: New civil service law is in force since 2009, 10 supporting regulations developed and enacted

title.narrative: Central civil service management instituted to enforce merit based recruitment and promote effective personnel management practices

baseline.value: Central civil service management capacity absent. Central oversight andenforcement of civil service legislation does not exist.

target.value: Central CS unit set up and its capacity to enforce civil service law and effective personnel policies created. Civil serviceregister is operational and enables effective oversight of personnel policies

actual.value: Personnel policy division established within the State Chancellery and is functioning. The capacity to enforce civil service lawand coordinate HR units is being developed through training and consultative support. Development of civil service register isclose to completion.

comment.narrative: Expected to be fully achieved with the launch of the civil service register.

title.narrative: Legislation on civil service and public administration, compatible with EU practice, approved and implemented

baseline.value: Civil service law (1995) does not require merit based competitive selection. The civil service management system is absent.Appointments are non competitive. A law on public administration absent

target.value: Civil service legislation approved and enforced. Public Administration is regulated by law.

actual.value: Both laws approved. New civil service law is in force since 2009. Implementing regulations for the civil service law fullydeveloped. Civil Service Classification and grading system developed and approved. Law on Public Administration approved in April2012.

title.narrative: (a) The institutional system is streamlined and consolidated around key policy areas, with Ministries playing a leading role in policy development and coordination of implementation.

baseline.value: Functions and legal status of government bodies are not aligned. Responsibilities for policy areas overlap. Legal regulation fororganization of public administration is absent

target.value: Delineation of policy and implementation functions complete at central government level

actual.value: The Government reorganization undertaken in winter-spring 2010 was guided by the functional review findings. In result,significantprogress was achieved in consolidating the institutional system around key policy areas. 130 Government decisionsrelated to reorganization were approved and 12 legal provisions were enacted by Parliament. The number of government agencies wasreduced from 16 to 8. Policy coordination units were created in the ministries and central agencies.

title.narrative: (b) The GO and the MoF coordinate and control the quality of Ministries' policy proposals within a rolling MTEF. Policy managementsystem established and functioning

baseline.value: No formal policy coordination mechanisms or institutional system are inplace. The MoEc is responsible for national planning. Newpolicies are approved regardless of fiscal implications

target.value: Institutional system, including policy units, central policy coordination, and methodologies are established and operational

actual.value: Policies, strategic planning and external assistance division established within the State Chancellery and is operational.Inter-ministerial Strategic Planning Committee established and is functioning. Policy Coordination Division plays a key role inpreparing MTEF , in close cooperation with the MoF. Special technical committees on the sector level are also established forfacilitation of anopen dialog during the MTEF preparation

comment.narrative: Largely achieved. The role of the State Chancellery in developing policy priority framework should be reflected in law to achievesustainability
